It details the construction of a ''Subjugator-class ship'' in the Enoth system.|Anakin Skywalker|{{TCWComicCite|6.54|Hotshot (comic story)}}}} The '''''Subjugator''-class heavy cruiser''' was a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] [[Warship/Legends|warship]] class that consisted of at least five ships. ==Description== ===Dimensions=== [[File:Malevolence_stern.png|thumb|left|180px|The ''Malevolence''{{'s}} stern, revealing its engine banks]] The [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy's]] most powerful [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]] class, it had some design similarities to both the [[Providence-class carrier/destroyer/Legends|''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer]] and the [[Recusant-class light destroyer/Legends|''Recusant''-class light destroyer]], but was almost as large as five [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]]{{TCW|Rising Malevolence|Rising ''Malevolence''}} - [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars#The Clone Wars: Decoded|Decoded]] and totaled 4,845 meters in length. The class was based around its [[Ion pulse cannon/Legends|ion pulse cannons]], a weapons system not used on board any other warship class, due to its unique power-generation needs. Despite its status as the Confederacy's most powerful battleship design, eclipsing pre-war models like the [[Lucrehulk-class battleship/Legends|''Lucrehulk''-class]], the model was classified as a heavy cruiser and was one of the largest designs that came from the Confederate shipyards. ===Offensive and defensive systems=== {{Quote|Looks like our intelligence was wrong—that ship's fully armed!|Anakin Skywalker|}} The battleship was fitted with the aforementioned gigantic [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]], which were charged with [[Plasma rotor/Legends|plasma rotors]] and fired a focused and directed ionic pulse at [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]], completely neutralizing their power systems. The weapon needed a significant cool-down period after each shot, to let ionized particles be cleaned out of the cannon before the next firing sequence. [[File:Malevolence_firing_ion_pulse.png|thumb|left|180px|The ''Malevolence'' firing its [[Ion pulse cannon/Legends|ion pulse cannon]]]] The ''Subjugator''-class was also armed with considerable amounts of standard secondary weaponry to destroy the ion cannon's victims.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/hnn/001.html#rss|text=HoloNet News — A Galaxy Divided|int=HoloNet News — A Galaxy Divided}} [[Turbolaser/Legends|Turbolasers]] were fitted to both its sides and dorsal superstructure, being clustered in large banks to defend against any ship that avoided the main ion cannons. They consisted of at least two different types: light and heavy dual turbolaser cannons.{{TCW|Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence''}} [[Proton torpedo/Legends|Proton-torpedo]] launchers were also part of the vessel's armament. The battleship was so massive that it could receive heavy turbolaser bombardment from multiple enemy capital ships without suffering any major damage, even with its shields disabled. Sixteen thrusters were positioned at the vessel's stern. However, it seems that the section connecting the ion cannon to the ship itself wasn't as durable, and bombardment to this area caused the weapon to overload during its firing sequence. [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] and his squadron attacked the [[Malevolence/Legends|''Malevolence'']] in this manner, resulting in the destruction of both ion cannons and considerable damage to the ship, knocking out its [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] as well as a number of other systems, shields included. ===Complement=== The warship carried several [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture''-class fighter]] and [[Hyena-class bomber/Legends|''Hyena''-class bomber]] squadrons, which could launch from multiple hangars on the side of the warship, right behind the ion array. The hangars had their own [[Firefighter droid/Legends|dedicated firefighting droid teams]], which could quickly respond to any emergency in the bays.{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode004.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Destroy ''Malevolence''}} The ship was large enough to have its own dedicated internal [[Rail jet/Legends|rail jet]] transportation system. The rails transported both passengers and materials on several levels and were connected with the various hangars. The rail-jet car design was similar to that of the [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transport]]. ===Bridge=== [[File:MalevolenceBridge-RM.png|thumb|left|200px|The ''Malevolence''{{'s}} bridge]] A communications array was located towards the stern, similar to the one found on the ''Providence''-class. The command center was also located in this tower, which had a multi-storied structure at the top, defended by multiple turbolaser batteries. This bridge contained a single raised platform in the center where the commander of the ship resided. A [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] terminal was present to allow the captain of the vessel to communicate with others. There were at least five circular computer screens with four stations in a semi-circular pattern where crew were stationed and controlled the mighty ship. Two [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolifts]] were at the back of the bridge, giving access to other levels in the ship. ==History== {{Quote|The ''real threat'' is far from here.''"
"''Yes, the Separatist mystery weapon.''"
"''Almost a dozen strikes now. Our fleet is being cut apart. And we're… ''here''.|Anakin Skywalker and [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]]|''[[The Clone Wars: Shakedown]]''}} [[File:Kaliida_Nebula_battle_plan.png|thumb|right|300px|A holographic representation of the ''Malevolence'']] The ''Subjugator''-class heavy cruisers were built in a [[Pammant Docks/Legends|shipyard]] orbiting the [[Quarren/Legends|Quarren]] world of [[Pammant/Legends|Pammant]]. Their construction was kept secret, with the simultaneous construction of the ''Providence''-class carrier/destroyer being used as a cover. The ''Malevolence'', designed by [[Ruggle Schmong/Legends|Ruggle Schmong]], served as Separatist [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous's]] [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] during the early months of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and destroyed dozens of Republic task forces before being destroyed by a joint effort of fighter strikes and internal sabotage.. The ''[[Subjugator (Subjugator-class)|Subjugator]]'' was built to carry [[trihexalon]] weaponry, and made it as far as Coruscant in its offensive, but was [[Trihexalon attack on Coruscant|destroyed]].''[[Kinect Star Wars]]'' The ''[[Devastation]]'', the sister ship of the ''Malevolence'', was involved in a conflict that concerned [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]] [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]].''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Jedi Alliance]]'' [[File:Grievousfist-ShadowofMalevolence.png|thumb|left|300px|General Grievous (pictured aboard the first ''Malevolence'') supervised the construction of a second vessel of the same name until its destruction at the hands of a Jedi Knight.]] A [[Malevolence (II)|rebuilt ''Malevolence'']] was also built at Pammant under the supervision of Grievous himself. However, it was subsequently also [[Mission to Pammant|destroyed]] by a [[Unidentified Jedi Knight (Clone Wars)|Jedi Knight]], who fought both Dooku and Grievous in the effort to destroy the second ''Malevolence''.{{TCWA|Card Commander}} A [[Unidentified Subjugator-class heavy cruiser|fifth ship]] was under construction at the [[Enoth system/Legends|Enoth system]] [[Unidentified Enoth system shipyards|shipyards]]. However, this ship was [[Battle of the Enoth system|destroyed]] by Skywalker and Tano's forces before its construction had been completed, striking a major blow to the Separatist cause. ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Malevolence_early_concept.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Early ''Malevolence'' concept]] The ''Malevolence'' was based on concept art for a Separatist [[communications ship]] meant to be used in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']]. The finished version was designed by [[Russell G. Chong]] and is based upon the [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|GR-75 medium transport]]. According to Director [[Dave Filoni]], the ''Malevolence'' and its story was based in part on the real-life German battleship [[Wikipedia:German battleship Bismarck|''Bismarck'']], which was hunted relentlessly by the British [[Wikipedia:Royal Navy|Royal Navy]] during World War II.{{SW|url=video/shadow-of-malevolence-episode-featurette|text="Shadow of Malevolence" Episode Featurette}} In the ''The Clone Wars'' episode "[[Shadow of Malevolence|Shadow of ''Malevolence'']]," Anakin Skywalker commands the [[BTL-B Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wing]] bombers to attack the starboard ion cannon, but the visuals show that it is the port cannon that is destroyed. The explosion takes out both cannons, however, making this statement moot. It is possible, however, that—due to either using the same power generator or really just being one, big, bidirectional cannon that can pick which side to fire from—the destruction of one caused a chain reaction that destroyed both guns, as well as extensively damaging to most of the ship. It could also be argued that Skywalker meant starboard in relation to the fighters during their attack run, which would have been ''Malevolence''{{'s}} port-side ion cannon. The destruction of the ''Malevolence'' by crashing into a moon echoes the fate of the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] by falling into the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star's]] gravity field. The [[in-universe]] argument over the ''Malevolence''{{'s}} size also mirrors the real-life arguments that were made about the ''Executor''{{'s}}. [[Henry Gilroy]] has suggested that the reason the ''Malevolence'' can receive holographic communications while in [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] is the size of the ship's internal gravity field.{{DHBoards|subdomain=www|url=Help/Boards/viewtopic.php?t=14536&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=61|text=The Clone Wars TV SHOW on Cartoon Network: WOWOWOW|nobackup=1}} (Fri Oct 10, 2008) In ''[[LEGO Star Wars III: The Clone Wars]]'', the character destroys the cannon by firing one torpedo into the cannon, instead of the many it took to destroy it.
